title: Superposition
description: Networks represent more features than dimensions using overlapping directions.

claims.heading: Toy networks superpose sparse features as near-orthogonal directions, with sparsity transitions and regular geometry
Are neurons polysemantic because features compete for limited capacity?
Polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure, so alone it is not evidence of superposition
Real models spread features across many neurons, or hold sparse features SAEs can recover
Are sparse autoencoder features complete, stable, canonical units of the model's representation?
Are superposed features one-dimensional directions rather than multi-dimensional structures?

related_findings.title: Interpretable sparse features in vision, biology and other domains
related_findings.summary: Sparse dictionaries trained on vision, biology, physics, recommendation and policy models can recover interpretable features. How selective, fine-grained and faithful those features are depends on the model, layer, dataset and evaluation.

examples.headline: In a pathology ViT, an SAE feature tracks plasma cells more selectively than a neuron.
A probe on DNABERT-2 SAE latents classifies CTCF-bound sequences at accuracy 0.7881.
ESM2-650M SAE features match ELM protein motifs at median AUROC 0.80, without neuron or random-model baselines.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Dictionary design choices set feature granularity
related_findings.summary: Dictionary architecture, width, sparsity, objective and preprocessing change which features are recovered, how fine-grained they are and how useful they are. No single setting does best on every criterion.

examples.headline: On MNIST, narrow high-L0 SAEs learn digit fragments; wide low-L0 SAEs learn whole-digit features.
On Gemma-2-2B, Matryoshka SAEs show far less feature absorption than TopK (0.056 vs 0.275).
Reconstruction-only SAE codes fail to separate author-level targets from background in Qwen.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Good reconstruction does not show meaningful features
related_findings.summary: Reconstruction, sparsity, coverage, stability and interpretability scores measure different things. None of them alone shows that a dictionary has recovered meaningful features, uses its capacity, or preserves task information.

examples.headline: Untrained random dictionaries cover a CUB concept-bottleneck model's concepts better than trained SAEs (0.65 vs 0.25).
SAEs reconstruct random-weight BiomedParse embeddings as well as learned ones; downstream AUC stays low.
A DiT SAE explains 0.9997 of variance while using only 1.5% of its dictionary.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: SAE features stay partly polysemantic and context-dependent
related_findings.summary: Dictionary latents and their labels need not match one stable human concept. How well a description predicts activations or effects varies with the examples, activation range, context and validation used.

examples.headline: Most sampled GemmaScope features had different input and output meanings (70.7% of 215).
Automated label misses a Gemma2-2B latent's secondary trigger, present in about 40% of top inputs.
Auto-interp descriptions predict ablation effects at ρ=0.69–0.81 on PRDB but only 0.36–0.62 on COLING.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Selected dictionary features can causally steer outputs
related_findings.summary: Selected SAE or crosscoder features can causally change generation, retrieval and policy outputs. The effects depend on which features are chosen, the model, the site, the strength and timing of the intervention, and gating.

examples.headline: Zeroing one SAE latent reorders retrieval; in one example, the top result falls to 9th.
Ablating top-10 culture-selective features cuts cultural MCQ accuracy to 0.31; random ablation does not.
Editing one feature in an SAE-tokenized recommender raises its exposure by 1.365 pp over controls.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Concepts spread across many units, directions and layers
related_findings.summary: A concept or behavior can depend on many neurons, directions, feature groups or layers that share, duplicate or compensate for each other's roles. These contributions shift under compression, pruning and scale.

examples.headline: Six coarse concepts stay linearly decodable in a width-128 distilled model, close to its teacher.
Optimized cones of directions flip truth answers; success varies by model and cone dimension.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Individual neurons range from narrow to mixed selectivity
related_findings.summary: Native neurons and adapter directions can be narrowly tuned, mixed or spread across variables. Measured selectivity depends on architecture, depth, context and method, and on its own does not show that limited capacity causes mixing.

examples.headline: 31% of inspected ResNet-18 neurons fire for unrelated concepts; 69% learn compositional abstractions.
Autointerp judges 62% of SAE latents on LoRA states monosemantic, versus 22% of LoRA directions.
Gemma-2-2B neurons selected by gradient-weighted activation change fire more densely than average neurons, with sharper peaks.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Architecture and training choices shape neuron specialization
related_findings.summary: Architecture, training method, objective, regularization, routing and pruning change a network's representation basis and how much its units specialize or share. This can happen even when the network is not short of units, and the effect on capabilities varies.

examples.headline: With L1/L2 penalties, a two-task network gives each neuron one task or leaves it unused.
Training models with k-winners-take-all self-ablation gives sparser SAE codes, more loss recovered, but higher weight L1.
MoWE (MoE with disjoint expert outputs) has more specific FFN coordinates than dense or MoE models.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Linear readouts expose concepts, with limits
related_findings.summary: Linear probes and vector differences expose semantic, factual and task information. Which axes are recovered and which shifts work depend on the model, layer, interface, context and controls.

examples.headline: In LLaMA-2-7B, word-pair differences align with a shared concept direction for 26 of 27 concepts.
A Qwen3-4B probe predicts code correctness at AUC 0.881; a prompt-length baseline reaches 0.657.
A weights-derived probe recovers Pythia 2.8B athlete-sport lookups at 98%, versus the model's 100%.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Features form semantic neighborhoods, families and hierarchies
related_findings.summary: Populations of dictionary features can form semantic neighborhoods, hierarchies and conditional or temporal families. How coherent they are depends on the model, selection and regularization, and statistical opposition is not the same as semantic opposition.

examples.headline: Selected neighboring SAE features form a semantic cluster with higher cosines than a random control.
Curated Qwen-VL-Chat SAE features on CLEVR form semantic-category blocks above random coherence.
Graph-learning AG-SAE assigns 23.55% of Gemma-2-2B child features multiple parents, with better-validated links than vanilla SAEs.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Decodable features are not necessarily good control handles
related_findings.summary: That a feature is decodable, active, selective or recurring does not make it a necessary or sufficient control handle. Causal effects depend on downstream readers, selection and context, and interventions can push activations off-distribution or cause broad damage.

examples.headline: Negative-multiplier SAE steering in SD v1.5 and SDXL Turbo yields 43–61% artifact rates.
Among SAE features that track person names, the most selective have the smallest causal effects (r=−0.56).
Gradient-based estimates predict the sign of single-latent ablation effects in 91–97% of cases; probes in 17–35%.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Concepts can live in multidimensional subspaces and manifolds
related_findings.summary: Concepts and task variables can occupy multidimensional subspaces, manifolds or structured feature families rather than single directions. Distinct variables can also share directions when read out by magnitude or nonlinearly.

examples.headline: Single linear-regression (TDR) axes predict motion and colour in context-dependent Mante-task RNNs; ablation barely changes accuracy.
On additive manifold mixtures, block-sparse featurizers recover blocks far better than TopK SAEs.
Gradient-reversal training against country drops linear-probe AUC to near-chance 0.519; an MLP probe still reaches 0.974.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Effective dictionary size can fall far below nominal width
related_findings.summary: SAE objectives, parameterization, preprocessing and data change dictionary coherence, feature identities, stability and how many latents are used. The usable set of features can differ greatly from the nominal width.

examples.headline: Top-k SAEs on sentence embeddings use most latents (few are dead), with little decoder-direction overlap.
A 2048-latent SAE on pathology embeddings uses only 74 latents across 7.7M patches.
GPT2-small attention-pattern transcoders keep only 144–524 of 2400 features alive.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Feature identities depend on how they are measured
related_findings.summary: Feature identity, polysemanticity and causal attribution depend on coordinates, decoder class, constraints, seeds, thresholds and controls. Stable statistics or subspaces need not mean the individual units are canonical.

examples.headline: ReLU decoding of 1-D antipodal codes nears R²=1 as sparsity grows; linear caps at 1/2.
In synthetic data, features sharing a rank-2 subspace seldom reappear across seeds, but the subspace does.
Steering projections correlate with log-mass contrast; reversing label–mass alignment nearly reverses the direction.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Dictionaries transfer imperfectly across data, models and updates
related_findings.summary: How well a dictionary covers and transfers depends on its training distribution, domain, modality, context, layer and model updates. Fidelity on source activations need not carry over to shifted activations.

examples.headline: Base-model SAEs transfer to longer contexts, with MSE up 12%, and to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct at most layers.
General-corpus SAEs explain less variance on domain and language data than on FineWeb-Edu.
Base-model Qwen-Scope SAE explains 0.50 of Instruct residual variance; an earlier 0.82 used the wrong hook.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Sparse codes help downstream tasks only in some settings
related_findings.summary: Sparse codes and feature selection can improve downstream readouts, correction or adjustment. The gains depend on task, layer, budget and baseline, and do not show a general advantage.

examples.headline: SAE profiles beat dense embeddings for RNA-type kNN at layers 5 and 11, not 0.
An adapter on driving-planner SAE latents cuts displacement error slightly more than dense or random-encoder inputs.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Models share some features, but alignment is partial
related_findings.summary: Different models can share partly alignable semantic structure while differing in individual directions. How much is shared depends on training, architecture, layer and matching method; shared geometry does not guarantee the features work interchangeably.

examples.headline: Two SAEs on the same CLIP-ViT-B/32 encoder align far above a shuffled control.
Features shared across models predict functional sites better than architecture-unique ones (AUROC 0.925 vs 0.661).
Cross-language SAE feature sharing is 87–96% in Gemma-3-4B but 4–6% in Llama-3.2-3B.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Steering effects depend on strength, context and combination
related_findings.summary: The effect of a feature intervention depends on its coefficient and sign, the context, how features are combined, and how the intervention is designed. It can also change behavior broadly, beyond the target.

examples.headline: Unscaled averages of coding steering vectors mostly yield refusals or jailbreaks; √n-scaling reportedly restores code output.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Encoder and inference choices change feature recovery
related_findings.summary: How well sparse features are recovered depends on encoder expressivity, inference procedure, optimization, geometry and benchmark design. Reconstruction quality alone does not certify recovery.

examples.headline: On GPT-2, dictionaries with MLP encoders score higher autointerpretability than SAE or LCA dictionaries.
LISTA-Matryoshka beats the best prior SAE on the synthetic SynthSAEBench-16k; LLM transfer is unverified.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Networks can compute nonlinear functions in superposition
related_findings.summary: Sparse superposed codes can support nonlinear computation. How accurate, how large and how deep that computation can be is limited by interference, readout, activation function, training objective and how labels are built.

examples.headline: Splitting neurons by Boolean clause gives 99.4% accuracy; dense networks with equal nonzero-weight counts get 78.7%.
Theory gives dimension thresholds ~k log m for pairwise conjunctions (k active of m random-dictionary features).
A hand-coded ReLU MLP holds 557 switchable vector-rotation circuits, but errors grow superlinearly with depth.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Sparsity objectives favor absorbed and mixed latents
related_findings.summary: Feature co-occurrence, hierarchy and sparsity objectives can favor absorbed or mixed latents even when the model is not short of capacity. Trained dictionaries, and fixes proposed for these problems, may not reach the best exact sparse code.

examples.headline: A closed-form L0 boundary for favoring parent over child features matches 30/30 synthetic, 12/16 trained-SAE settings.
A feature-mixing (hedging) SAE beats a truncated true-feature SAE on MSE at k=4 (0.42 vs 0.53).

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Features persist, drift and recur across layers
related_findings.summary: Features can persist, shift, merge or reappear across layers. Single-layer reconstructions and decoder norms can miss token-dependent drift between layers, and the same feature repeated at several layers.

examples.headline: Multi-layer SAE features spread across layers in aggregate (variance ratio 54–88%) but not per token (1–10%).
Bishop-move features recur at three chess-model layers; ablating one does little, masking all lowers target-move probability.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Representations keep dense, anisotropic and basis-aligned structure
related_findings.summary: Distributed representations can keep dense, anisotropic, low-rank or coordinate-aligned structure. Effective dimension and basis preferences depend on architecture, site, depth and method.

examples.headline: Usually, attention outputs have effective rank about 60% of width; MLP and residual streams about 90%.
Sampled Qwen3-32B layer-0 neurons are heavy-tailed, and kurtosis tracks lexical concentration (ρ=0.55).
Toy-model hidden dimensions have more interdependent signs (mutual information) than the authors report for real transformers.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Small feature sets can stand in for dense representations
related_findings.summary: Small sets of dictionary features can preserve local neighborhoods, selected task information or the effect of a behavioral direction. How many features are needed, how faithful the substitute is, and whether it transfers depend on inputs, task, dictionary and the sparsity imposed.

examples.headline: An adaptive mask keeping about 40 SAE concepts matches dense CLIP reconstructions in test-time training.
In Phi-3 Mini, 2–4 SAE features rebuild an effective refusal direction; sycophancy is harder.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Reconstruction and replacement can lose task information
related_findings.summary: Reconstructing activations, or replacing model parts with sparse ones, can lose task information. Fidelity varies with layer, domain, repeated encoding and the replacement architecture.

examples.headline: Layer-24 SAEs reconstruct other layers poorly; Gemma's fraction of unexplained variance reaches 24.05 at layer 41.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Features emerge and reorganize during training
related_findings.summary: Feature emergence, rotation, consolidation and geometry change over training. Inferred transitions and the strength of superposition depend on the objective, input statistics and measurement method.

examples.headline: Toy-model Bayesian posterior shifts from pentagonal to hexagonal feature arrangements at 600–700 samples, as theory predicts.
A forced random superposition bottleneck gives power-law loss-decay exponents near 1 mid-training, as learnable embeddings do.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Feature interventions change outputs beyond text models
related_findings.summary: Interventions on dictionary features can change outputs in biological, vision, recommendation and control models. Selectivity, side effects and effectiveness vary by architecture, stream, layer and concept.

examples.headline: In the GTRS driving planner, zeroing three SAE latents raises overall score but lowers route progress.
In implicit neural representations, ablating one SAE atom hurts SIREN reconstructions locally, Fourier-feature MLP ones image-wide.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Feature roles change with depth and model scale
related_findings.summary: Dictionary features differ in token alignment, abstraction, role, dynamics and sharing across depth and model scale. Features emerge, split and persist unevenly.

examples.headline: In a small LM, deeper SAE features are less concept-selective: top concepts lead runners-up by less.
French and German backdoor-trigger features overlap in 13 of 27 layers (8B model), none at 1B.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Geometry encodes values, but measures need task-specific checks
related_findings.summary: Concept geometry can encode hierarchies and continuous values. Similarity, orthogonality and dimension need task-specific metrics and controls before they can predict recovery, causal equivalence or independence.

examples.headline: Steering along a learned time manifold shifts year completions, working best around layers 8–14.
A LoRA-learned direction and a mean-difference direction are nearly orthogonal, yet their downstream effects partly align.
In synthetic settings, signal-to-noise ratio and alignment predict target-direction recovery; intrinsic dimension does not.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Feature pathways reveal reuse and separate meanings
related_findings.summary: Tracing features through upstream pathways can separate the meanings of a polysemantic unit and expose compositional reuse. Circuit connectivity and decompositions depend on training, basis and analysis.

examples.headline: In two ViT-B neurons, unrelated concepts share 18% of upstream pathways, related ones 42%.
A training-time decorrelation penalty cuts the downstream components reading each concept from about 21 to 1.4.
Pythia 2.8B still recalls athletes' sports with later attention mean-ablated; an MLP-only version reaches 94% accuracy.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Features persist or drift as models keep training
related_findings.summary: Dictionary features can persist across model updates, but their activations, geometry and causal roles can drift with continued training, fine-tuning and pruning.

examples.headline: Across Pythia training, broad early SAE features persist far more often than narrow ones.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Sparse features expose task and reward signals
related_findings.summary: Sparse features can expose task-relevant, demographic or reward-related signals and support targeted interventions or training constraints. Their selectivity depends on context and model.

examples.headline: Zero-ablating GPT-4-flagged features lowers reward in two Pythia models but not GPT-Neo-125m.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Multimodal models mix shared and modality-specific features
related_findings.summary: Multimodal representations can contain both shared and modality-specific components. Alignment and transfer depend on token modality, layer, thresholds and post-training, and features that fire together need not point the same way.

examples.headline: SAE latents labeled multimodal range from 23 to 223 depending on the threshold.
Aligned text-side SAE directions steer LLaVA captions at layer 25; an unaligned SAE at matched sparsity never succeeds.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Overlapping features and interventions do not add simply
related_findings.summary: Overlap between features can predict spillover from interventions, but behavioral effects need not combine independently or additively. Reducing global correlation between dictionary atoms need not reduce the interference that actually occurs.

examples.headline: Low-interference training cuts overlap between dictionary atoms 19.2%, but overlap weighted by their activations only 0.9%.
Modeling pairwise interactions between steering directions predicts their combined MMLU-Pro effects better than summing individual effects.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Attention heads and weights can multiplex several functions
related_findings.summary: Attention heads and weight components can carry several functions at once or spread one function across many components. Intervention effects depend on capacity and inputs, and these findings alone do not show superposition in activations.

examples.headline: In Gemma-2b, individually helpful head knockouts don't add: the top 3 together beat the top 10.
In a four-head toy model learning five skip trigrams (A…B→C), one was spread across all heads.
Ablating head L1H6 turns off 443 of 450 induction features and hurts other code features.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Supervised and compositional objectives reshape dictionary features
related_findings.summary: Supervised, task-aware and compositional training objectives can change which latents represent each concept and can improve some semantic or recovery measures. They do not establish canonical atomic features.

examples.headline: Meta-SAEs trained on decoder directions explain 42% of Matryoshka SAE decoder variance but 55% for BatchTopK.
An SAE trained for predicting CLIP's errors yields more directions humans judge to match one class.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: SAE codes shift with context and small perturbations
related_findings.summary: Which SAE features fire, and what they represent locally, can change with context, paraphrase, time and perturbations. Stability depends on thresholds, position, depth, training objective and model.

examples.headline: Only 11.7% of SAE features for bare concept names survive in contextual prompts.
GCG attacks perturbing one token cut top-k SAE feature overlap with the original to about 20–30%.
Noun latents silenced by added adjectives often fire upstream; most are near threshold, except in Mistral.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Supervised subspaces can beat neurons and SAE units
related_findings.summary: Supervised subspaces and alternative decompositions can isolate task variables better than single neurons or unsupervised SAE units in some settings.

examples.headline: On Llama-3.1, supervised subspaces found by DAS beat SAE featurizers on RAVEL entity-attribute and multiple-choice tasks.
A training-free sign dictionary from unembeddings nearly matches a Gemma Scope SAE on sparse probing.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Graph-level descriptions can work without canonical atoms
related_findings.summary: Encoder and decoder proxies can misdescribe what a feature does mechanistically. Graph structure and downstream metrics can still give predictive descriptions without relying on canonical individual SAE atoms.

examples.headline: SAE-encoding every Gemma 2 steering vector, even a zero vector, gives the same top two features.
Attribution-graph structure predicts probe accuracy (Gemma ρ=0.91), but in Llama only weakly within a concept.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Feature frequency and training conditions shape dictionary allocation
related_findings.summary: Prevalence, co-occurrence, variance, scale and learning conditions affect how strongly features are represented and how dictionaries allocate latents. There is no universal rule that frequent features get dedicated units.

examples.headline: 76% of a layer-8 residual-stream SAE's features fire on single-token inputs; authors blame imbalanced training n-grams.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Attention computation runs through sparse, low-rank channels
related_findings.summary: Attention computation and communication between modules can be broken into sparse or low-rank parts. The relevant dimension depends on feature type, normalization and downstream readout.

examples.headline: Llama 3.1-8B heads filter categories with rank-1 query-key subspaces; binding by word identity needs rank 9–10.
Attention-pattern transcoders for GPT2-small permit only 25,000–51,000 of about 69 million possible query-key feature pairs.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Features can be shared across languages or language-specific
related_findings.summary: Features can be shared across languages or specific to one. Their activation and causal effects depend on concept, task, depth, linguistic context, resource level and training.

examples.headline: Ablating two language-specific SAE directions mainly hurts the target language in Gemma 2 and Llama-3.1.
In Gemma-2-2B, SAE activations are lower on text translated into lower-resource languages than on high-resource-language text.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Overlapping codes accompany retrieval failures and forgetting
related_findings.summary: Overlapping codes and competing contextual states can come with worse retrieval, composition and retention. The size of the effect depends on training coverage, state weighting, feature strength and update conditions.

examples.headline: Reweighting superposed reasoning states lowers a trained router's success and raises false alarms on inactive keys.
Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-1.5B on facts causes far more forgetting when keys are meaningful rather than random UUIDs.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Superposition geometry predicts adversarial vulnerability
related_findings.summary: The interference geometry of superposed features can predict adversarial vulnerability and transfer. How robustness training changes this depends on geometry, task, capacity, layer and attack type.

examples.headline: In toy models, adversarial vulnerability correlates with features per dimension (r≈0.99) under Elhage et al.-style attacks.
Toy-model robust accuracy falls as k/m (features per bottleneck dimension) rises, reaching 18.7% at m=2.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Networks damp or amplify perturbations depending on direction
related_findings.summary: Networks suppress or amplify perturbations unevenly across directions and can favor candidate feature directions over mixtures of them. Apparent error correction depends on direction, layer, dictionary and baseline.

examples.headline: In a two-layer denoising network, perturbation-response exponents are higher along true feature directions than feature mixtures.
Parent SAE features amplify slightly more than children, but SAE features are not local maxima.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Code geometry sets capacity and loss scaling
related_findings.summary: How much a representation can store, and how loss scales, depend on code geometry, learned embeddings, how many features are active at once, and the superposition regime.

examples.headline: Learned embeddings merge inputs that share an output, cutting the dimension needed for error-free recall.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: MoE experts mix specialized and shared functions
related_findings.summary: Mixture-of-experts experts and routes can combine specialized and shared functions. How semantically broad an expert is depends on routing sparsity, layer, granularity and interacting features.

examples.headline: In gpt-oss-20b and OLMoE, each expert's top SAE latents span fewer semantic clusters than random sets.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Refusal follows one direction; harmfulness has more structure
related_findings.summary: Refusal can be strongly driven by one dominant linear direction, while harmfulness and behavior categories keep additional, overlapping structure that depends on the method.

examples.headline: Harmfulness subcategory directions have effective rank 1, yet probes retrained after directional ablation stay accurate.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Vision embeddings partly compose by vector addition
related_findings.summary: Some vision and text-to-image embeddings support approximate vector composition and separate word senses, while similar concepts and attributes can blend or interfere.

examples.headline: Composite-image MedCLIP embeddings are rebuilt from component embeddings at cosine similarity 0.97.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Vision activations cluster meaning locally; findings depend on method
related_findings.summary: Semantic structure in vision activations shows up in local regions of activation space, at class boundaries and in scene components shared across channels. What is found also depends on the analysis or reconstruction method.

examples.headline: Images reconstructed from deep-layer channels share a large component; subtracting the cross-channel mean mostly removes it.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Population directions predict brain responses better than units
related_findings.summary: Directions across a population can be more interpretable, or better predictors of biological visual responses, than individual artificial or biological units.

examples.headline: Sparse-autoencoder latents predict fMRI in the human ventral visual stream better than ResNet50 and ViT neurons.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Compressed and distilled students do not fully match the teacher
related_findings.summary: Adapting a model can make a fixed feature dictionary describe it more faithfully. A student distilled at equal or smaller capacity need not recover the teacher's units, and its loss can level off above zero.

examples.headline: Distilled Pythia-410M students plateau at a nonzero KL divergence from the teacher, even at teacher width.

related_findings.title: Toy models store data points in superposition
related_findings.summary: Toy bottleneck networks can store individual training examples in superposition, and can shift from memorizing examples to learning features. Whether and how double descent shows up depends on training conditions.

examples.headline: Weight decay removes the double-descent test-loss bump between memorizing and learning features; more epochs enlarge it.

reading_list.why: The original toy-model study: feature sparsity and importance shape superposition and its geometry. Read phase diagrams with the linear comparison.
A second toy model (quadratic), analyzed and simulated, showing when features get their own dimension, share dimensions, or are ignored.
Shows in a toy autoencoder that polysemanticity can arise incidentally, without capacity shortage; prevalence in real models is open.

known_gaps.summary: Main open problems: thin evidence at large scale; unresolved or merely apparent disagreements about feature reproducibility, geometry and interpretability; challenges that are counterexamples rather than failed replications; unread or unverified sources; possible new claims whose independence is unchecked; and misread findings and duplicate records not all fixed.
items: Little of the evidence comes from models above 10B parameters, and no study is recorded above 100B. Many studies do not state model size, so conclusions about scale rest on very few studies.

Studies disagree on how reproducible SAE features are across training seeds in GPT-2 small: one matches 94% of latents, another finds much lower reproducibility. The two appear to use different dictionary widths, so the gap may reflect width rather than a failed replication.

Several challenges to the claims are counterexamples to strong wording, not failed replications. For instance, polysemanticity without a shortage of neurons shows that capacity shortage is not necessary, not that it is never sufficient.

Possible disagreements between studies on the same models have not been worked through. Examples are circular weekday features versus a one-dimensional pattern for years in GPT-2 small, which may differ only in the feature studied, and SAEs scoring near chance on word senses versus positive interpretability results.

Part of the literature could not be checked: 65 candidate studies could not be retrieved, and parts of the original paper's findings and of Bricken et al.'s sparse-autoencoder study remain unverified. Two relevant studies, one on seed stability by Paulo and Belrose and one arguing that superposition is not necessary, have not yet been assessed against the claims.

Some large groups of findings may deserve claims of their own, notably computation in superposition, the link between superposition and adversarial vulnerability, and multidimensional features. Whether these findings come from independent research groups has not been checked.

A check of the study findings recorded here found many misreadings, and only those flagged in the summaries were corrected. Duplicate entries for the same study and missed overlaps between author groups also make it unclear how independent the evidence is.
